name: Kano
blurb: Ancient city, dye pits older than your great-grandfather, and the best kilishi you will ever eat.

events.text: Your PPA is a secondary school in Kano. The students call you 'Corper Teacher' and correct your Hausa with great patience. By month six you can haggle at Kurmi market.
A Kano trader you befriended offers you a small consignment of leather bags to resell in Abuja. Good margin, if you can move them.

name: Enugu
blurb: Coal City. Rolling hills, abacha on every corner, and uncles who ask what you are doing with your life.

events.text: Your PPA boss in Enugu runs a printing press and teaches you how to price jobs properly. 'Never do business with family on credit,' he says, then sells to his cousin on credit.
A landlord in Enugu demands rent in advance even for corpers. You negotiate down with a CDS certificate and pure audacity.

name: Lagos
blurb: Somehow, against all odds, you got Lagos. Traffic is a lifestyle. Everyone has three jobs.

events.text: In Lagos you share a mini-flat with four corpers in Yaba. The tech scene is wild. You sneak into a startup meetup and leave with two job leads.
Third Mainland Bridge traffic eats four hours a day. You start making skits about it. One goes viral.

name: Rivers
blurb: Port Harcourt: Garden City, oil money, generator noise and the best bole and fish.

events.text: Your PPA is an oil-servicing company. You watch people make in a week what your parents made in a year. You take notes.
Soot from illegal refineries settles on your white shirts. A local NGO recruits you for a clean-air campaign.

name: Benue
blurb: Food Basket of the Nation. Yam, rice, and hospitality that embarrasses Abuja.

events.text: You teach agricultural science in a Benue secondary school. A farmer explains more about supply chains in an afternoon than your lecturer did in a semester.
Your CDS group builds a small borehole for a village. The chief gives you a goat. You do not know what to do with a goat.

name: Cross River
blurb: Calabar: clean streets, carnival season, edikang ikong that changes lives.

events.text: Calabar carnival season. You volunteer and end up dancing in a costume with feathers. Your Instaflex grows by 2,000 followers.
Your PPA is a hotel. You learn hospitality, and you learn that tourists tip in dollars.

name: Ogun
blurb: Next to Lagos, cheaper than Lagos, full of factories and Lagos workers who sleep there.

events.text: Your PPA is a factory in Ota. You learn production planning and how to survive on 'staff canteen' rice.
You start selling Adire fabric to your Abuja friends online. Small orders, steady orders.

name: Kogi
blurb: Where the Niger meets the Benue. Lokoja's confluence view is free; the roads are not smooth.

events.text: The Abuja–Lokoja road is an adventure novel. You spend one Friday night in traffic behind a fallen trailer and make three friends.
Your PPA is a local government office. Your job title is 'Assistant'. Of what, nobody knows.

name: Abia
blurb: God's Own State. Aba's markets make anything you can imagine, and some things you can't.

events.text: Your PPA is a shoe factory in Aba. You learn how 'Made in Aba' becomes 'Made in Italy' with one label. The craftsmanship is real, though.
An Aba tailor makes you two native outfits for the price of one Abuja shirt. You look like money for the rest of the year.

name: Adamawa
blurb: Mountains, the Benue river, and Yola's hot, slow afternoons. Fura da nono at every junction.

events.text: You teach at a girls' secondary school in Yola. Your best student wants to be an engineer. You help her apply to university.
A CDS trip to the Sukur highlands. Ancient stone terraces, cold wind, and the best photographs you will ever take.

name: Akwa Ibom
blurb: Uyo is clean, calm and full of good food. Afang soup might change your life.

events.text: Your PPA is the state ministry of information. The roads are smooth, the offices are cool, and the work is light.
A corper friend's mother teaches you to cook afang and edikang ikong. You will never respect Abuja buka soup again.

name: Anambra
blurb: Onitsha main market, Nnewi spare parts, and the most serious traders in West Africa.

events.text: You serve at a trading company in Onitsha. Your oga can price a container of goods in his head faster than you can on a calculator.
An Nnewi spare-parts dealer offers you a small cut to find buyers in Abuja. You make a few sales.

name: Bauchi
blurb: Yankari Game Reserve, Wikki warm springs and wide open skies.

events.text: Your CDS group takes a trip to Yankari. You swim in the Wikki warm spring and see elephants for the first time.
You teach maths at a rural school. The students walk five kilometres to class. You stop complaining about Abuja traffic.

name: Bayelsa
blurb: Yenagoa, creeks, boats instead of buses, and fresh fish pepper soup.

events.text: Your PPA is reached by boat. Every morning you put on a life jacket like it's a seatbelt. You learn to love the creeks.
Flood season. Your lodge takes water and you move in with a family who treat you like their own child.

name: Borno
blurb: Maiduguri, the city that has survived everything. Corpers are posted to the safer capital, and the welcome is warm.

events.text: You serve at a general hospital in Maiduguri. You see more courage in one week than in your whole life.
Your landlady sends you dates and kilishi every Friday. 'You are far from home,' she says. You are not, anymore.

name: Delta
blurb: Warri no dey carry last. Sharp people, sharp jokes, and banga soup.

events.text: Your PPA is an oil-servicing company in Warri. The staff speak pidgin faster than you can think. You learn fast.
A Warri 'businessman' tries to recruit you into a scheme. You laugh him off. He laughs too. Nobody is fooled in Warri.

name: Ebonyi
blurb: Abakaliki rice, salt lakes and the friendliest landlords in the South East.

events.text: You serve at the state's rice mill. You learn how paddy becomes the rice on your plate. You'll never waste rice again.
Your community throws a party for the corpers. You eat so much abacha you skip dinner for two days.

name: Edo
blurb: Benin City: bronze casters, ancient walls and loud, proud people.

events.text: Your PPA is a secondary school in Benin City. On weekends you visit Igun Street and watch bronze casters work like their ancestors did.
Every other person you meet has a cousin in Italy. You get very good at saying 'no thank you' to travel agents.

name: Ekiti
blurb: Fountain of knowledge. Quiet hills, serious professors, and pounded yam with everything.

events.text: You teach at a school where the principal wants every student in university. Your lessons are watched closely.
A retired professor in your street lends you books every week. You read more this year than in all of university.

name: Gombe
blurb: Jewel in the Savannah. Peaceful, green, and the cheapest rent you'll ever pay.

events.text: Rent is so cheap you save almost your whole allawee. Your bank account has never looked healthier.
You start a free evening computer class for secondary school leavers. Twenty students sign up.

name: Imo
blurb: Owerri: nightlife, shopping and some of the best hotels outside Lagos.

events.text: Owerri nightlife is everything they said. Your allawee disappears faster than you planned.
Your PPA is a private hospital. You help with records and patients. The doctor says you'd make a great administrator.

name: Jigawa
blurb: Dutse's rock formations, farms as far as you can see, and people who greet you three times.

events.text: You teach English at a rural school. By month three your students are reading story books aloud.
Your neighbours insist you join them for meals every evening. You put on weight and lose all your loneliness.

name: Kaduna
blurb: The old capital of the North. Big roads, big markets and Kaduna polo on weekends.

events.text: Your PPA is a state government agency. Files move slowly, but the director takes a liking to you.
A Kaduna textile trader shows you how the market works. You flip some fabric in Abuja for a small profit.

name: Katsina
blurb: Ancient city walls, the Gobarau minaret and very generous hosts.

events.text: Your host family treat you like their own. By the end of the year you speak conversational Hausa.
You teach at a girls' school and help run a debate club. They beat a school from Kano in the state finals.

name: Kebbi
blurb: Argungu fishing festival country, rice farms and long quiet evenings.

events.text: You're there for the Argungu Fishing Festival: thousands of fishermen jump into the river at once. Unforgettable.
Your PPA is an agricultural project. You learn how Kebbi rice gets to Abuja markets, and who takes the profit.

name: Kwara
blurb: Ilorin: calm streets, amala, and a place where everybody seems related.

events.text: Your PPA is the state broadcasting corporation. You present a youth show on Saturday mornings.
Ilorin is so peaceful you sleep eight hours every night for the first time since secondary school.

name: Nasarawa
blurb: Next door to Abuja. Lafia's yams, salt flats and the chance to visit Abuja on weekends.

events.text: You're posted to Keffi, an hour from Abuja. You spend weekends in Abuja making connections for after service.
Your PPA is a farm settlement. You learn how yams are stored and sold. Real agribusiness.

name: Niger
blurb: Minna: the hills, the dam at Shiroro, and suya on every street.

events.text: You teach at a school in Minna. Your students are curious about Abuja and ask you a hundred questions a day.
A CDS trip to the Gurara Falls. You stand in the spray and forget all your wahala.

name: Ondo
blurb: Akure, cocoa farms and the beaches of Ilaje.

events.text: You serve at a cocoa cooperative. You learn how farmers get cheated by middlemen, and how to stop it.
You visit Idanre Hills and climb all 682 steps. Your legs never forgive you. Your Instagram does.

name: Osun
blurb: Osogbo: the sacred grove, artists everywhere, and a slow, creative pace.

events.text: Your PPA is an art gallery in Osogbo. You learn how artists price, sell and ship their work abroad.
You attend the Osun-Osogbo festival. The colours, the drums, the crowd. You write about it and it goes viral.

name: Oyo
blurb: Ibadan: brown roofs, Bodija market, and the oldest university in Nigeria.

events.text: Your PPA is a research institute at the University of Ibadan. A lecturer offers to supervise your master's someday.
Ibadan is huge. You get lost in Dugbe market twice and come out with good deals both times.

name: Plateau
blurb: Jos: cool weather, rocks everywhere and strawberries. The closest thing Nigeria has to a hill station.

events.text: The cool Jos weather makes you feel like you're on holiday all year. You walk everywhere and get fit.
A Jos potato farmer asks you to help with his books. You find money he didn't know he was losing.

name: Sokoto
blurb: The seat of the Caliphate. History, hospitality and very, very hot afternoons.

events.text: The heat is serious, but so is the hospitality. Your host family adopts you completely.
You teach at an Islamiyya-and-western-education school and run a reading club in the evenings.

name: Taraba
blurb: The Mambilla Plateau: tea plantations, cattle and cool green hills.

events.text: You visit the Mambilla Plateau. Tea fields, cool mist and fresh milk. You don't want to leave.
Your PPA is a health centre in Jalingo. You help with a vaccination drive that reaches three villages.

name: Yobe
blurb: Damaturu: quiet, dusty and full of people who make you feel at home. Corpers serve in the capital.

events.text: You teach at a school that lost years to insecurity. The students are hungry to learn. So are you.
A local trader teaches you the cattle and grain business. You understand Nigeria's food chain for the first time.

name: Zamfara
blurb: Gusau: farmland, gold rumours and very patient people. Corpers serve in the capital.

events.text: You serve at the state secretariat. Paperwork is slow, but you learn how government really works.
Everyone has a story about gold. You decide not to chase it. A wise decision.
